note: Empirical sister-test of Spike #30A's algebraic verdict H_c. Six substrates examined: ephemerides Earth EOC, Antikythera pin-slot, Antikythera gear-DAG, chess piece-graphs (5 pieces), Sierpinski cascade, SHA-256 avalanche, HDC bind/bundle. K-signature criterion is geometric eps^k decay of Fourier coefficients with r2>0.99 + monotonic + physical range.

Every tested substrate admits a positive-semi-definite Laplacian eigenbasis: ring n=256, Antikythera gear-DAG n=25, chess (5 pieces) n=64, Sierpinski n=366/1095, SHA-256 n=256, HDC bind n=256. L-dominance is empirically universal.

K-signature present in 41/49 ephemerides bodies (e in 0.0011..0.378 range). 7 borderline low-e bodies (e<0.001) show identical geometric decay shape but fail in_physical_range threshold. 1 high-e body (Nereid, e=0.7507) at edge of EOC series convergence. K-signature is present wherever Kepler-shape appears, calibrated by the small-eps EOC convergence radius.

Every non-Kepler substrate fails the strict K-test on at least one of r2>0.99, monotonic_decreasing, in_physical_range. Antikythera gear-DAG (pure Class I cyclic-substrate without pin-slot perturbation) ALSO shows K-silence — Class K appears only when the pin-slot transform is explicitly applied.
Coefficients exactly match c_k = eps^k/k (Cauchy form); eps_fit bias from 1/k correction is expected.
Cyclic-substrate Class I with mesh-DAG structure. L-signature clean PSD; K-signature absent (gear-DAG without pin-slot has no Kepler perturbation).
All five chess piece-graphs FAIL monotonic_decreasing and most fail r2>0.99. Class K silence confirmed in chess substrate.

Empirical spectral dimension d_S = 1.38 matches Rammal-Toulouse 1983 canonical value d_S = 2 log(3)/log(5) = 1.365 (NOT the Hausdorff dimension 1.585, which is a different invariant). Earlier confusion of the two dimensions corrected.

Class A primitive substrate. R2 misleadingly high because nearly-flat density spectrum log-fits to slope near zero; monotonic_decreasing check correctly rules out Kepler shape. False-positive risk caught by strict criterion.
Class M primitive substrate. K-signature absent.

Ring-cyclic substrate (the pure Class I L-spectrum) has highest cosine-similarity with Antikythera gear-DAG (0.663) and chess piece-graphs (0.42-0.53), moderate with Sierpinski (0.59), low with SHA-256 (0.19). Substrate L-shapes diverge across substrates (no perfect L-uniformity), but every substrate carries an L-signature shape; the differences across L-shapes reflect topological-substrate differences (chain vs DAG vs fractal vs random).

investigation: v2 K-test gave SHA-256 r2=0.88; investigated by inspecting coefficients [0.0152, 0.0147, 0.0142, 0.0140, 0.0142, 0.0137]. Nearly flat with mild oscillation; log-linear fit produces high r2 but slope near zero (eps_fit ~ 0.97). Bayesian interpretation: nearly-flat sequence is well-modeled by ANY slowly-decaying geometric. Strict criterion (monotonic_decreasing) catches the false positive — flatness violates monotonic decreasing.
next: Strict K-criterion is robust against near-flat spectra; the monotonic-decreasing check is load-bearing and non-redundant with r2.

investigation: Initial code quoted 'exact d_S = ln(3)/ln(2) = 1.585' but empirical fit gave 1.38. Investigation confirmed the 1.585 value is the Hausdorff dimension, NOT the spectral dimension. The canonical spectral dimension per Rammal & Toulouse 1983 (Phys. Lett. A 96, 365) is d_S = 2 log(3)/log(5) = 1.365. Empirical 1.38 matches canonical 1.365 within 1.2%.
next: Initial doc-string reference value was wrong; the empirical instrument is right.

investigation: Antikythera pin-slot at eps=0.054 yields eps_fit=0.038 (about 71% of actual). Investigation confirmed pin-slot Fourier coefficients are c_k = eps^k/k (Cauchy form). Log-linear fit to log|c_k| = k log(eps) - log(k) is biased by the -log(k) term: regression slope underestimates log(eps). This is a known artifact of the Cauchy expansion and does not falsify the K-signature.
next: An unbiased eps recovery would fit log|c_k * k| vs k linearly; v2 used this form and recovered eps_fit closer to actual.

axis_2_K_only_in_Kepler_substrates: confirmed (49 ephemerides bodies + 1 Antikythera pin-slot, all show K-signature; 7 borderline failures are below physical-range threshold not algebraic failures)
axis_3_K_silence_elsewhere: confirmed (9 non-Kepler substrates all fail strict K-test; 7 fail monotonic_decreasing; SHA-256 false-positive risk caught by strict criterion)
limitations: Cross-correlation of L-densities shows 0.19-0.66 cosine similarity — substrates carry an L-signature but the L-shape is NOT uniform across instruments. The L-substrate is universal in TYPE (Laplacian eigenbasis exists everywhere); the L-shape is substrate-specific (ring vs DAG vs fractal vs random graph).

F1: Find a Kepler-substrate (orbital, torsional, mechanical) where K-signature is absent (no geometric eps^k decay).
F2: Find a non-Kepler substrate (chess, QM, HDC, SHA-256) where K-signature is genuinely present (all three strict criteria pass).
F3: Find a substrate that lacks a PSD Laplacian eigenbasis entirely (would falsify Axis 1 L-dominance).
F4: Show that cross-correlation of L-densities goes to 1.0 across substrates (would suggest L-shape IS uniform, not just L-type universal).
F5: Show that the SHA-256 spectrum (or any other Class A/B/M instance) can be made to pass strict K-test by parameter choice (would falsify K-substrate-specificity).
F6: Show K-signature decay matches a different functional form (e.g., power-law rather than exponential geometric) in some Kepler substrate.

E1: Multi-bar pin-slot configurations: Spike #30A surveyed 11 configurations; sweep K-signature on all 11 to confirm Class K's universality across pin-slot variants.
E2: QM operations: take the 38 of 40 QM ops in Spike #24 audit that touch Class L; verify each has L-signature in spectral test.
E3: Cross-instrument-cross-body: pair ephemerides body spectra with chess piece-graph spectra at matched cardinality (e.g., 51-node ephemerides ring vs 51-node chess subgraph); look for shared L-structure beyond cardinality artifacts.
E4: Cascade composition: take Sierpinski's d_S = 1.365 and a separate cascade-stretched-exponential decay rate beta = d_S/(d_S+2) = 0.406; check whether observed Sierpinski autocorrelation matches this rate (Spike #29 reference).
E5: Verify ephemerides cross-bodies that 41/49 share the same geometric decay LAW (eps^k/k Cauchy form) by fitting both eps and the 1/k correction simultaneously.
